channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: I Used NYT Cooking’s New AI-Powered Recipe Modifier, and It’s Actually Pretty Good
item.description: NYT Cooking recently launched an AI-powered feature for recipe scaling and unit conversion, aimed at simplifying prep work. Despite intense backlash in the comment section over 'smart kitchen' fatigue, the feature has proven surprisingly reliable and functional in real-world usage.

item.title: The inventor of the bitter lesson has a bitter lesson for LLM scaling enthusiasts
item.description: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton argued on social media that raw compute scaling alone won't lead to AGI. He criticized the reliance on synthetic data, advocating for AI agents that move beyond static internet text and learn continuously through complex real-world interactions.

item.title: Inside Inner Mongolia, China's fastest-growing AI data center region, where construction is accelerating with low building cost and no public backlash (SemiAnalysis)
item.description: Inner Mongolia's Ulanqab is becoming the epicenter of China's AI infrastructure, with massive gigawatt-scale data center clusters under construction. The region delivers projects at one-fifth the cost of US counterparts with lightning speed, leveraging policy and geographic advantages without the public backlash seen in the West.

item.title: World Models Will Soon Be Inescapable. Here’s What You Need to Know
item.description: Niantic, the creator of Pokémon Go, has shifted its focus from AR gaming to developing 'world models' using their proprietary spatial data. Unlike LLMs, this technology processes visual input to predict real-world physics, aiming to serve as the critical training ground for home robotics and autonomous vehicles by 2027.

item.title: AI coding agents still need human cleanup on nearly three out of four tasks in a real-world test
item.description: Researchers from Alibaba and affiliated universities introduced the Co-Design Bench to test AI coding agents on real-world web application modification tasks. The results reveal that even the top-performing models achieve a success rate of only 26.4%, shattering the illusion of perfection seen in previous, saturated benchmarks.

item.title: Major environmental groups are embracing AI to analyze climate data, track forest fires, and more, even as they warn of the environmental impact of data centers (Valerie Volcovici/Reuters)
item.description: Global environmental groups are increasingly deploying AI to analyze complex climate models and monitor forest fires. Simultaneously, they are raising alarms about the massive carbon footprint and water consumption of data centers, urging a balance between innovation and ecological sustainability.

item.title: Internal documents leaked by Cisco workers angry over the company's ties to Israel's military show how it expanded its business as the war in Gaza dragged on (Alice Speri/The Guardian)
item.description: Disgruntled Cisco employees leaked confidential internal memos protesting the company's military ties. The documents reveal that Cisco's network infrastructure for the Israeli military suffered from persistent, critical system failures during the conflict, severely undermining the client's confidence in the provider.

item.title: The crypto industry is bracing for a reckoning after Democrats won the US midterms and vowed to investigate the Trump family and its ties to the industry (Financial Times)
item.description: Following the Democratic victory in the U.S. midterms, party leaders vowed to launch a sweeping investigation into the Trump family, specifically targeting their intricate ties to the crypto industry. This move aims to dismantle the former president's political funding channels by exposing potential regulatory and ethical breaches within these crypto alliances.

item.title: Nous Research unveils Arete-27B, a post-trained Qwen3.8-27B model that reinforces Western values, saying the underlying Chinese model's bias layer is shallow (Nous Research)
item.description: Nous Research has developed Arete-27B by post-training Alibaba's Qwen2.5-27B. The team aims to overlay Western values onto the base model, arguing that it is necessary to mitigate existing state-aligned biases in the original Chinese-trained weights.

item.title: Beijing-based GenRobot AI, which develops equipment and software for collecting human demonstrations that can be used to train robots, raised a $100M Series A+ (TechNode)
item.description: Beijing-based GenRobot AI has raised $100 million in a Series A+ round, backed by investors like SAIC and Baidu. The company specializes in building data infrastructure for robotics, using custom hardware and software to capture human movement data for training.

item.title: Filings: Apple saved $2.7B in taxes this year by routing up to $50B in profits through Singapore, exceeding the $2.6B in tax savings it achieved via Ireland (Financial Times)
item.description: Apple shifted $50 billion in profits through Singapore to secure $2.7 billion in tax savings, officially surpassing its previous tax shelter in Ireland. This strategic move highlights how multinational giants are navigating global tax pressures by relocating financial structures to more favorable jurisdictions.

item.title: How a small, wealthy AI-safety network that organized in Signal chats grew into a coalition that beat the $100M super PAC Leading the Future in the midterms (Politico)
item.description: A coalition of wealthy AI safety advocates coordinated via Signal to successfully outmaneuver a well-funded super PAC during recent midterm elections. This shift signals that AI safety has evolved from academic theory into a high-stakes political battleground for regulatory dominance.

item.title: US Treasury moves to cut crypto exchange MEXC off from the US financial system, alleging $16B+ in illicit flows, including Russian and Iranian sanctions evasion (Francisco Rodrigues/CoinDesk)
item.description: The U.S. Treasury has moved to sever the crypto exchange MEXC from the U.S. financial system. The action targets over $16 billion in illicit flows, specifically citing the platform's alleged role in helping Russia and Iran evade international sanctions.

item.title: Report: SEA makes up ~50% of APAC data center capacity being built, led by Malaysia and Thailand, which paused 49 and delayed approvals of 117 projects in Sept. (Arundhati Hazra/The Guardian)
item.description: The data center building boom in Southeast Asia has hit a wall, with Thailand and Malaysia pausing or delaying 166 projects in September. The move stems from severe power and water constraints, coupled with growing government concerns over regulation and monitoring.

item.title: Public records appear to show SpaceX building a "Starbase supercomputer" in TX, but Gina Hinojosa's election as governor may delay some of the data center plans (Ann Davis Vaughan/The Information)
item.description: Elon Musk moved early to build AI data centers in Tennessee and Mississippi and reaped the rewards.

item.title: Binance says CFO Kaiser Ng is leaving to "pursue a new venture" days after a $6.3B hack, citing a six-month transition plan, and names Justin Yek as CFO (Bloomberg)
item.description: Binance CFO Kaiser Ng has announced his resignation to pursue new ventures. The move comes just days after the world's largest crypto exchange suffered a $6.3 billion hack, with a six-month transition period planned as Justin Yek takes over the role.

item.title: Anthropic pushes ahead with pre-Thanksgiving IPO despite tech selloff, accepts lower valuation
item.description: Anthropic is pressing ahead with its IPO despite the tech selloff, accepting a lower valuation. The Claude developer wants to go public before Thanksgiving and raise $80–100 billion at a $1.25–1.75 trillion valuation, according to investors cited by the Financial Times. That tops the current $965 billion but falls short of the $2 trillion the most optimistic investors had hoped for. item.title: Exponential Time Hypothesis co-proposer Russell Impagliazzo calls OpenAI's disproof "shocking news"; it could one day speed up chip design and break encryption (Cade Metz/New York Times)
item.description: A longstanding hypothesis held that some problems would always be hard for computers to solve quickly.

item.title: AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood reviewers with false alarms, new study finds
item.description: AI models can often spot problematic behavior by other AI agents in logs. But the harder they try to catch every case, the more harmless actions they flag as suspicious. That makes them better suited for estimating how often things go wrong than for safety checks that need to reliably catch every single incident. item.title: Democratic wins could slow AI investment and safeguard the US economy against a downturn by pacing it over time, as Deutsche Bank sees "shaky" projects killed (Cecile Daurat/Bloomberg)
item.description: Guardrails against data-center expansion in states won by Democrats may help spread investment over time.

item.title: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small drops 316 F-bombs across benchmark runs
item.description: Researchers found that the Inkling 2 model by Thinking Machines frequently outputs profanity in its chain-of-thought logs. When the model hits dead-end logic or experiences system failures, it generates aggressive outbursts, though these hidden reasoning steps are rarely visible to end-users.

item.title: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
item.description: Around 7PM each weeknight, I find myself standing in front of the fridge, trying to decide on something for dinner that won’t make my husband complain, “Chicken again?” Yes, I should meal plan more, but I don’t, so this is where I’m at. A nightly battle in which the chicken usually wins. Recently, my best weapon in this fight has been AI. item.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
item.description: Several Chinese firms approved to import high-end Nvidia AI chips were found to have vacant offices and ties to sanctioned entities. Despite approval by the US Department of Commerce, investigations reveal some of these companies barely exist, casting doubt on the efficacy of export vetting.

item.title: The gap between open and closed AI models in cyber capabilities keeps shrinking
item.description: Recent benchmarks reveal that open-weights models like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reach 72.8% success in simulated network attacks, closing the gap with closed-source models. Since open models cannot be restricted, experts warn that the window for effective cyber defense is narrowing rapidly.

item.title: Chicago-based data analytics company Ocient raised a $100M Series C co-led by Boka Capital and OCA Ventures to grow its agentic AI analytics business (Paul Gillin/SiliconANGLE)
item.description: Ocient Inc., the maker of a speedy data analytics platform, today said it has raised $100 million in a Series C funding to expand …

item.title: Investigation: some Chinese companies approved by the US Commerce Department to handle Nvidia's H200 chips have empty offices and ties to firms under sanctions (New York Times)
item.description: The Commerce Department has approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, some of which have ties to firms under sanctions over national security.

item.title: State propaganda in some Chinese AI models is only "a thin layer" that fine-tuning can strip away
item.description: US startup Nous Research fine-tuned Alibaba's Qwen2.5-27B model to create a new version called Arete-27B. By injecting specific datasets, the team reduced the original model's propaganda output rate from 22% to under 1%, aiming to strip away embedded national narratives.

item.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
item.description: Anthropic is using AI to build more powerful AI. And it appears to be working remarkably well, with the company's models improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with little indication of slowing down. That's according to a new report published Thursday by the AI safety research organization METR, following an 11-week investigation inside the company, as part of a report evaluating its AI research and development. item.title: Nasscom President Rajesh Nambiar warns AI could make it harder for fresh Indian engineering graduates to find jobs, urging an immediate CS curriculum overhaul (Sayan Chakraborty/Nikkei Asia)
item.description: The president of India's top tech industry body warned that AI automation is displacing entry-level coding and testing roles, making it harder for fresh grads to land jobs. He urged an immediate overhaul of CS curricula to align with the new AI-driven reality.
